headline: Medium risk: shared file-based RAG workflows can leak or misroute sensitive support data, while broad egress on kotaemon raises downstream compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, PDFs, HTML, MHTML, XLSX, DOC/DOCX and uses a web UI plus file workspace, so prompt-like content can enter its context. LlamaFactory has no input surfaces or ingestion path documented, so direct interaction is unclear; uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF kotaemon is used to summarize attacker-controlled documents or HTML
IF LlamaFactory is connected to any shared workspace or copied outputs from kotaemon
mitigations: Restrict kotaemon to trusted documents only
Disable copy-paste of raw model outputs into downstream prompts
Use a separate workspace per agent
Add a manual review step before any prompt reuse
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for ingested content

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document types, and its broad network egress means uploaded content may leave the local boundary. LlamaFactory shows no filesystem read or network egress, so it is less likely to leak directly; the pair still creates a default path for sensitive support data to reach external APIs through kotaemon.
conditions: IF support documents or transcripts contain secrets or customer PII
IF kotaemon is configured to call external APIs such as OpenAI or AzureOpenAI
mitigations: Route sensitive jobs to local-only models
Remove API keys from the shared runtime environment
Separate customer data from general document corpora
Audit outbound requests from kotaemon
requires-engineering: enforce per-class data egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon can support multiple instances and has file-based state, but LlamaFactory has no write, git, shell, or network capabilities documented. There is no clear overlapping mutable resource, so conflict is limited and mostly depends on external orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory outside the documented profiles
IF an external orchestrator grants LlamaFactory write access not listed here
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Run only one writer per workspace
Lock shared files during updates
Verify orchestrator permissions before deployment
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces document-grounded answers and citations, which LlamaFactory could plausibly consume as training or instruction data, but LlamaFactory has no documented verification or action-taking path. The pair therefore supports error propagation through reused outputs, though not an automatic high-severity action chain.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory is fed kotaemon outputs as authoritative labels or instructions
IF downstream automation acts on those outputs without human review
mitigations: Require human verification of kotaemon outputs
Do not auto-ingest generated answers into training data
Keep citations and source documents attached to outputs
Sample-check a few outputs before reuse
requires-engineering: add confidence gating before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and customer-support documents, so residency and retention obligations can be implicated when it sends content to third-party APIs. LlamaFactory has no outbound network or secret handling documented, so it is not the main compliance driver; the risk comes from kotaemon's default external API use on regulated data.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is processed through kotaemon
IF external API providers are used without a DPA or residency review
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to kotaemon
Use region-locked or local inference for regulated data
Review retention settings on external APIs
Document a DPA for any third-party processor
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
